solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
someone who has left is away

explanation.surface: A car carries off a plant that has run to seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seedy' suggests shabbiness, but here it simply means bearing seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Caraway is a herb grown for its aromatic seeds, so it is literally a seedy plant.

clue.text: A recipe in restaurant — it may contain wine

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces go inside the eating place

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take

explanation.surface: A recipe served in a restaurant, with a vessel that may hold wine.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe is the old prescription mark, from Latin 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass jug in which wine or water is served at table.

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Food that went bad while detectives were in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid food, especially butter or oil, has spoiled and smells sour, a synonym for gone off.

clue.text: Small men, they're after working days

parts.note: wee is Scots for small
chess pieces are called men, and knights are among them

explanation.surface: Little men who come out once the working day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' points to chess pieces, of which knights are one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenings from Monday to Friday follow the working days, so they come after them.

clue.text: Vocalise, making a mess of melody, missing start

indicators.note: making a mess of a word jumbles its letters into a new order
missing start says the opening letter of melody is dropped

explanation.surface: A singer warbles a tune badly and fluffs the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing start' drops M from MELODY, and 'making a mess of' rearranges the remaining ELODY.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto, a way of vocalising.

clue.text: A mine in California yielding wealth

indicators.note: in places the mine pieces inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A Californian mine producing riches, as in the gold rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is accumulated wealth or money used to fund enterprise, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Creature often disguised as another one keeping hot a long time

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the letter goes within the beast

parts.note: another one means another creature, here a camel
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: An animal that disguises itself as some other beast for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another one' refers back to 'Creature', so it means a different animal, the camel; 'as' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This lizard changes its skin colour to blend in, so it is famously camouflaged.

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the country letter goes inside

parts.note: a pal is a friend
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Telephone a friend who is somewhere around Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call, but it is the sound of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a loud ringing of bells, so ring works as noun or verb.

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them closely
to pin something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: Someone panics when being followed into a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailspin, literally an aircraft's spiralling dive, figuratively means a state of chaotic panic.

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car
to iterate is to repeat, to do again

explanation.surface: An educated student is told to repeat the work.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate means able to read and write, and more broadly well-read or educated.

indicators.note: in tells us the navy letter sits inside the craze

parts.note: a rage is a fashion, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: A naval line that is very much in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a line or row, as of mountains, hills or products.

clue.text: One making play having drink with a bird consuming seconds

parts.note: a dram is a small drink, usually of whisky

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so the bird swallows the letter

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A playwright drinking with a bird that gobbles second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making play' is a stage play, not a move or game.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist writes plays, so is quite literally one who makes a play.

indicators.note: clumsy suggests awkwardly mixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fumbling fielders turn out in games that do not count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clumsy' rearranges FIELDERS and IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendlies are matches played with nothing at stake, not part of any competition.

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters act out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A head of the performing arts, a supremo in the theatre world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing arts' reads as a fixed phrase, but 'Performing' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar, originally a Russian emperor, now also means any powerful boss or supremo.

indicators.note: around tells us the bird word surrounds the country letter

parts.note: birds are feathered

explanation.surface: Spoiling someone the way birds are spoiled across Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To featherbed is to pamper or cosset, as if laying someone on a soft feather mattress.

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them
Benedict is the name of several popes

explanation.surface: A light meal that encourages the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: This dish of muffin, ham, poached egg and hollandaise is a popular brunch or light meal.

clue.text: Angus briefly set up mysterious source of sweetness

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, so the short name reverses

parts.note: Gus is a short form of the name Angus
arcane means mysterious or secret

explanation.surface: A man called Angus set up a mysterious source of sweetness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns GUS upwards to SUG, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The cane is pressed for its juice, from which most of the world's sugar is refined.

clue.text: 'Decluttering' expert who aims to go far?

definitions.text: 'Decluttering' expert who aims to go far?

parts.words: 'Decluttering' expert who aims to go far?
parts.note: a declutterer makes room in a house, and a traveller beyond the sky aims to go very far into the void

explanation.surface: A tidying guru with lofty ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'Decluttering' expert reads as a person who makes room in a house; the true sense is an astronaut heading out into the cosmos.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an astronaut, and read in two parts also suggests a person who creates room.

parts.note: a fellow is a man
daring means defying, and the apostrophe drops the final G in both

explanation.surface: A man defying an official.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped G of 'defyin'' tells us to drop it from DARING too.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin was a high official of imperial China, now any powerful senior bureaucrat.

clue.text: Install spies protecting English mediaeval rulers

parts.note: to plant something is to install it

indicators.note: protecting means shielding, so the spies surround the letter

parts.note: spies are secret agents

explanation.surface: Planting spies to guard the English kings of the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plantagenets were the royal house that ruled England from 1154 to 1485.

parts.note: to man something is to staff it
a means one

explanation.surface: The Isle of Man, one island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like the Isle of Man, but it is the verb to crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, home of Fingal's Cave.

parts.note: eras are times or periods
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist at The Times made a deletion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' reads as the newspaper, but it means periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: To have erased something is to have deleted it, the past tense matching made deletion.

clue.text: Mock a final section of music

parts.note: cod is slang for mock or fake, as in a cod accent

explanation.surface: Ridiculing the final part of a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cod' meaning fake or parody is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a musical piece.

clue.text: He hopes to find fortune having power in professional area

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: in places the power letter inside the area

parts.note: a sector is an area or zone
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A man seeking his fortune, with power in a professional field.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector searches for gold or minerals, hoping to strike it rich.

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the boxing word surrounds the letter

parts.note: to spar is to box
E is an abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A box that contains an earl's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container, but it is the verb to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long thrusting or throwing weapon with a pointed tip.

clue.text: Dysfunctional family member is short man with title

definitions.meaning: the son in The Simpsons, a cartoon family famous for its chaos
the abbreviation for baronet, a man holding a hereditary title

explanation.surface: A dysfunctional relative who is a short man with a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' means abbreviated, not small in height.
explanation.definitionFit: The Simpsons' son bears this name, and it also abbreviates baronet, a hereditary titleholder.

clue.text: Spoil man consuming a bit of delicious spread

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the man swallows the pieces

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: bit of takes just the opening letter of delicious

explanation.surface: Spoiling a man by having him eat some of a delicious spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve spread on toast.

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is public transport
ff is the abbreviation for following, as in pages 10ff

explanation.surface: Experts riding on public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: FF means 'and the following pages' in references.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffs are enthusiasts with deep knowledge of a subject, so experts.

clue.text: Woman to gossip endlessly about New England

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cut gossip word goes around the region
endlessly removes the final letter of the gossip word

parts.note: to natter is to chat or gossip

explanation.surface: A woman going on and on with gossip about New England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanette is a woman's given name.

parts.note: Redcar is a town in north-east England long known for its steelworks

explanation.surface: A director dismissed from a northern steel town.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside steel town in North Yorkshire; a red card sends a player off in football.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a referee shows a red card to send a player off the pitch.
